issues.body: check_workflow classifies only workflow/job/step env mappings and the github-script `github-token` input. A label writer such as `run: GH_TOKEN=${{ secrets.MAINTAINER_PAT }} gh pr edit "$N" --add-label needs:user` has an inline mutation but an empty `effective` mapping, so the loop emits no offence. The same gap applies to a secret passed as a command argument or Authorization header. This directly defeats the claimed border: the workflow can still write a label under a maintainer PAT while the gating check passes.
issues.fix_hint: Inspect executable `run`/github-script text for credential expressions and assignments used by label-writing commands, rejecting any non-approved secret or unprovable token source. Add a self-test for an inline `GH_TOKEN=${{ secrets.MAINTAINER_PAT }}` label write that must fail. If complete shell data-flow analysis is intentionally out of scope, narrow the documented invariant and add a separate enforceable restriction that forbids credential expressions in label-writer bodies.
issues.title: Inline credential expressions bypass token attribution

issues.body: classify_token returns success for every non-expression value unless it happens to match a small GitHub token-prefix regex. Thus token-shaped fields such as `GH_TOKEN: $MAINTAINER_PAT`, `GH_TOKEN: opaque-token`, or a token format not covered by that regex pass, despite the documented rule that a present credential must be provably github.token or an App token. This is fail-open and also makes the hard-coded-token detection dependent on incomplete prefix recognition.
issues.fix_hint: For any token-shaped env/input being classified, reject every non-empty value that is not syntactically proven to be an approved expression; only empty values should pass without an approved source. Add negative fixtures for a shell-variable value and an arbitrary literal, plus a positive fixture only if there is a legitimate non-expression form that can be proven safe.
issues.title: Unprovable literal token values are accepted

verdict.summary: The new gate is fail-open for credential forms that its stated invariant says must be rejected. In particular, a label-writing step can place a PAT expression directly in its run/script body, or assign a literal/shell-expanded value to a token-shaped environment variable, and the checker reports no offence. The fixtures cover only mapping-based `${{ secrets.* }}` credentials, so they do not expose these bypasses.
